title: Attendance at group pelvic floor muscle training classes among referred women: barriers and associated factors
subtitle: Design not yet settled: survey of referred women or review of referral records
statement: Fewer than half of the women referred to group pelvic floor muscle training for stress urinary incontinence attend the first class, and about a quarter complete four or more of six sessions. The service does not know which factors are associated with attending or what stops women from coming, and needs that knowledge before redesigning the classes.
whoAffected: About 1,100 women a year referred with stress urinary incontinence after childbirth or in midlife, especially younger mothers, women living far from the hospital and women who need an interpreter; the physiotherapists who run the classes.
whatHurts: Women who do not attend keep leaking urine, avoid exercise and social activity, and may later need surgery; classes run half empty while the waiting list grows.
currentPractice: Daytime six-week group classes at the hospital; referral letters are the only record of why a woman might not attend, and reasons are not asked.
whyNow: The service wants to redesign its programme, and an impression that younger, distant and interpreter-dependent women drop out has never been checked.
constraints: No research funding; printing and postage up to 1,500 from the service budget. Survey materials in English and the two most common other languages of referred women. No extra clinic appointments for the study.
patientCenteredGoal: Women referred for stress urinary incontinence can take part in pelvic floor training at a time, place and in a language that fits their lives.
summary: Problem framed; the design is left open (survey or records review) until the evidence is reviewed.
